extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates studying algebraic topology / homotopy theory
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, structural properties, and basic theorems about homotopy groups (absolute and relative), plus core CW-complex techniques (cellular approximation, compression lemma, CW approximation) used to compute and manipulate these groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of πn(X,x0)
rubrics_metrics.description: πn(X,x0) is the set of homotopy classes of maps f:(In,∂In)→(X,x0) with homotopies required to satisfy ft(∂In)=x0. For n=0 take I0 a point so π0(X,x0) = set of path-components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently view elements as homotopy classes of based maps (S^n,s0)→(X,x0) by collapsing ∂In to a point; homotopies must be through maps fixing the basepoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Group operation on πn for n≥1 (and abelianity for n≥2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sum operation (f+g) is defined by splitting the first coordinate of In into left/right halves, yielding a well-defined group structure for πn(X,x0) when n≥1. For n≥2 the group is abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identity is the constant map, inverses given by precomposing with (s1↦1−s1). The abelian homotopy between f+g and g+f uses sliding disjoint subcubes past each other (requires n≥2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Basepoint-change isomorphisms
rubrics_metrics.description: For a path γ from x0 to x1 there is a change-of-basepoint map β_γ:πn(X,x1)→πn(X,x0) defined by inserting γ in a shell; β_γ is an isomorphism with inverse β_{γ^{-1}}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Properties: γ(f+g) ≃ γf + γg, (γ η)f ≃ γ(η f), and 1 f ≃ f. Hence for path-connected X one writes πn(X) independent of basepoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: π1-action on higher πn (module structure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The assignment [γ] ↦ β_γ defines an action of π1(X,x0) on πn(X,x0), making πn a module over the group ring Z[π1(X,x0)]; elements of Z[π1] act by finite sums ∑ n_i γ_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology: 'n-simple' means trivial π1-action on πn; 'abelian' in this book means trivial π1-action on all πn. Nilpotent refers to nilpotent π1 and nilpotent action. H-spaces give examples of abelian spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality of πn
rubrics_metrics.description: A map ϕ:(X,x0)→(Y,y0) induces ϕ_*:πn(X,x0)→πn(Y,y0) by ϕ_*([f])=[ϕ f]; ϕ_* is a homomorphism for n≥1 and respects composition and homotopy of ϕ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If ϕ is a homotopy equivalence it induces isomorphisms on all πn (even if basepoints move during the homotopy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Covering space behavior (Proposition 4.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If p:(	ilde X,	ilde x0)→(X,x0) is a covering projection then p_*:πn(	ilde X,	ilde x0)→πn(X,x0) is an isomorphism for all n≥2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses lifting criterion (surjectivity) and covering homotopy property (injectivity). Consequence: if X has contractible universal cover then πn(X)=0 for n≥2 (aspherical spaces).

rubrics_metrics.name: Product formula for πn (Proposition 4.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an arbitrary product of path-connected spaces ∏_α X_α, there are isomorphisms πn(∏_α X_α) ≈ ∏_α πn(X_α) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A map into a product is the same as a collection of maps into factors; apply with Y=S^n or S^n×I to see functoriality in homotopies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of relative homotopy groups πn(X,A,x0)
rubrics_metrics.description: For n≥1, πn(X,A,x0) is the set of homotopy classes of maps (In,∂In, J_{n-1})→(X,A,x0), equivalently maps (D^n,S^{n-1},s0)→(X,A,x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition uses the coordinate s_n (so group for n≥2, abelian for n≥3). For n=1 the set is paths in X from varying point in A to x0 and typically not a group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression criterion for triviality in relative groups
rubrics_metrics.description: A map f:(D^n,S^{n-1},s0)→(X,A,x0) represents zero in πn(X,A,x0) iff it is homotopic rel S^{n-1} to a map with image contained in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use deformation retraction to constant map in A to show triviality; conversely, a nullhomotopy can be reparametrized to produce a homotopy into A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence of a pair (and triple)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a long exact sequence ...→π_n(A,x0) →^{i_*} π_n(X,x0) →^{j_*} π_n(X,A,x0) →^{∂} π_{n-1}(A,x0) → ... → π_0(X,x0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: i and j are inclusions; ∂ is boundary map (a homomorphism for n>1). Exactness interpreted as image = kernel, even in the non-group end where 'constant map class' is the zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness proofs and naturality
rubrics_metrics.description: Exactness is proved by compression criterion and homotopy constructions; the sequence is natural: maps of triples induce maps between long exact sequences with commuting squares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The triple long exact sequence generalizes the pair case. Verifications at the low-degree end (π0 etc.) are left as exercises but follow the same image-kernel logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: n-connectedness (absolute)
rubrics_metrics.description: A based space X is n-connected if π_i(X,x0)=0 for all i ≤ n. Equivalent conditions: (1) every map S^i→X is nullhomotopic for i ≤ n; (2) every map S^i→X extends to D^{i+1}; (3) π_i(X,x0)=0 for all x0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 0-connected = path-connected; 1-connected = simply-connected. Basepoint choice irrelevant when n≥0 because of path-connectedness conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative n-connectedness (pair criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a pair (X,A) the following equivalent (for i>0): (1) every map (D^i,∂D^i)→(X,A) is homotopic rel ∂ to a map D^i→A; (2) every such map is homotopic through such maps to a map D^i→A; (3) every such map is homotopic through such maps to a constant map D^i→A; (4) π_i(X,A,x0)=0 for all x0∈A. For i=0, conditions (1)-(3) say each path-component of X contains points in A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair (X,A) is n-connected if these hold for all i ≤ n (with appropriate interpretation at i=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Whitehead's theorem
rubrics_metrics.description: If f:X→Y between connected CW complexes induces isomorphisms f_*:π_n(X)→π_n(Y) for all n, then f is a homotopy equivalence. If f is inclusion of a subcomplex X↪Y then X is a deformation retract of Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses the compression lemma and mapping cylinder arguments. Important caveat: isomorphic homotopy groups alone (without a map inducing them) do not guarantee homotopy equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression lemma (Lemma 4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (X,A) be a CW pair and (Y,B) any pair with B≠∅. If for each n with cells of X−A we have π_n(Y,B,y0)=0 for all y0∈B, then every map f:(X,A)→(Y,B) is homotopic rel A to a map X→B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proved inductively by homotoping characteristic maps of cells into B using the vanishing hypothesis, then extending via homotopy extension property; works with infinite-dimensional cell sets by a limiting homotopy trick.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension lemma (Lemma 4.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a CW pair (X,A) and a map f:A→Y with Y path-connected, f extends to X if π_{n-1}(Y)=0 for all n such that X−A has cells of dimension n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inductive proof: extension over an n-cell exists iff the composition of the attaching map S^{n-1}→X^{n-1} with f is nullhomotopic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular approximation theorem (Theorem 4.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every map f:X→Y of CW complexes is homotopic to a cellular map (f(X^n)⊂Y^n for all n). If f is cellular on a subcomplex A, the homotopy may be kept stationary on A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof proceeds cell-by-cell by making images miss higher-dimensional cells (using compactness to meet finitely many cells) and iterating; use technical Lemma 4.10 to create local PL structure to avoid entire cells. Consequence: many dimension-based arguments (e.g. π_n(S^k)=0 for n<k) follow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary πn(S^k)=0 for n<k (Corollary 4.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Using cellular approximation with standard CW structures on spheres, every basepoint-preserving map S^n→S^k is homotopic to a cellular map, hence constant if n<k; thus π_n(S^k)=0 for n<k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate corollary of cellular approximation (fix basepoint as 0-cell).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical lemma to deform maps into a cell (Lemma 4.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f:In→Z where Z is obtained from W by attaching a cell e^k, there is a homotopy to f1 and a polyhedron K⊂In such that (a) f1(K)⊂e^k and f1|K is PL in some identification e^k≅R^k, and (b) K⊃f1^{-1}(U) for some nonempty open U⊂e^k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in the cellular approximation proof to produce points p in e^k missing the image of f1 when n<k. Construction uses subdivisions, PL linearization on simplices, and uniform continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cellular approximation for pairs and fixed-subcomplex refinement (Example 4.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every map of CW pairs f:(X,A)→(Y,B) can be deformed through maps of pairs to a cellular map; homotopy may be stationary on any subcomplex where f is already cellular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply cellular approximation to A→B first, extend, then cellularly approximate the extension while fixing A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectivity of (X,X^n) and consequences (Corollary 4.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: A CW pair (X,A) is n-connected if all cells in X−A have dimension > n. In particular (X,X^n) is n-connected, so inclusion X^n ↪ X induces isomorphisms on π_i for i<n and a surjection on π_n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from cellular approximation applied to maps (D^i,∂D^i)→(X,A) with i≤n and the long exact sequence of the pair.

rubrics_metrics.name: CW approximation existence and construction (Proposition 4.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every space X has a CW complex Z and a weak homotopy equivalence f:Z→X (a CW approximation). If X is path-connected, Z can be chosen with a single 0-cell and cells attached by basepoint-preserving maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construction is inductive: attach cells to kill kernels and realize homotopy groups step-by-step so that at stage k the map is injective on π_{k-1} and surjective on π_k. Use only generators where possible to be efficient. CW approximations are unique up to homotopy equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: CW approximation for pairs and relative weak equivalence (Example 4.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given (X,X0) one can produce a CW approximation (Z,Z0)→(X,X0) extending a CW approximation Z0→X0 so that f:(Z,Z0)→(X,X0) induces isomorphisms on relative as well as absolute homotopy groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach cells to Z0 mapping into X to create a weak homotopy equivalence; apply five-lemma to deduce relative isomorphisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability and computation focus: reduce to p-torsion
rubrics_metrics.description: The complexity of homotopy groups of spheres resides in finite abelian groups; π_i(S^n) is finite for i>n except for π_{4k-1}(S^{2k}) which has a Z direct summand. Thus the problem reduces to computing the p-torsion in π_i(S^n) for each prime p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freudenthal suspension theorem gives stability along diagonals (π_{n+k}(S^n) eventually independent of n for large n). Use Hurewicz theorem for first nonzero homotopy ≅ first nonzero homology.
